item.title: Guardians force a decisive Game 5 against the White Sox
item.description: Cleveland erased another elimination threat with a 9-5 win in Chicago, powered by homers from José Ramírez and Patrick Bailey and a six-run sixth inning. The ALDS returns to Cleveland for Saturday’s Game 5, with the winner advancing to face Tampa Bay.

item.title: MLB proposes 154-game season and a revamped postseason
item.description: Major League Baseball proposed cutting the schedule from 162 to 154 games in 2029, expanding the Division Series to seven games and letting higher seeds choose playoff opponents starting in 2027. The players union said the package remains tied to MLB’s push for a salary cap.

item.title: Stankoven’s first hat trick powers Carolina’s rout
item.description: Logan Stankoven recorded his first NHL hat trick and Andrei Svechnikov scored twice on the power play as Carolina overwhelmed Vancouver 7-2. Sean Walker added four assists, another career first, as the Hurricanes won their third straight.

item.title: Rays sweep Yankees and advance to the ALCS
item.description: Victor Mesa Jr. broke a tie with a two-run homer as Tampa Bay beat New York 4-3 to sweep the ALDS. A fan-interference review erased what initially appeared to be Anthony Volpe’s tying homer, leaving the Yankees short and sending the Rays to their third ALCS.

item.title: Brewers finish Padres and earn an NLCS rematch
item.description: Milwaukee beat San Diego 3-1 in Game 4, ending a 12-game postseason road losing streak and setting up a second straight NLCS against the Dodgers. Jackson Chourio supplied the go-ahead single, while Garrett Mitchell robbed Manny Machado of a potential tying homer.

item.title: Oilers score five in one period to stun the Ducks
item.description: Edmonton erased a 2-0 deficit with five unanswered second-period goals in a 5-2 win at Anaheim. Leon Draisaitl had four assists, Evan Bouchard scored twice and Connor McDavid added a goal and two assists as the Oilers improved to 3-0-1.

item.title: Yamamoto strikes out 10 as Dodgers regain NLDS lead
item.description: Yoshinobu Yamamoto allowed one run in seven innings and struck out a postseason-career-high 10 as Los Angeles beat Atlanta 3-1 for a 2-1 NLDS lead. Enrique Hernández and former Brave Freddie Freeman homered in the fourth; the Dodgers can clinch a third straight trip to the NLCS with one more win.

item.title: Padres stave off elimination and force Game 4
item.description: Jake Cronenworth broke a tie with a fifth-inning homer and Michael King earned a six-out save two days after starting as San Diego beat Milwaukee 4-3. Xander Bogaerts ended the game with a sharp double play, keeping the Padres alive and extending the Brewers’ road postseason losing streak to 12.

item.title: World Cup winner Pedro retires after a 20-year career
item.description: Pedro Rodríguez retired at 39 after 794 club appearances, 197 goals and 25 major trophies. The versatile forward won the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012 with Spain, collected 20 trophies at Barcelona and later won the Premier League with Chelsea before finishing his career in Rome with Roma and Lazio.

item.title: Falcons run over Saints in 45-24 Monday night rout
item.description: Bijan Robinson broke a 59-yard touchdown on Atlanta’s third play and joined Brian Robinson for five rushing scores as the Falcons beat New Orleans 45-24. Atlanta moved to 2-2 and into a tie for the NFC South lead. Michael Penix Jr. completed 15 of 20 passes for 223 yards and a touchdown.

item.title: Rays seize 2-0 ALDS lead after Yankees unravel
item.description: Tampa Bay used a four-run fifth inning and pressure throughout the lineup to beat New York 5-2 and move one win from the ALCS. The Yankees committed three errors in the first inning, and the Rays later chased ace Cam Schlittler with a parade of contact, speed and aggressive baserunning.

item.title: White Sox rally to move within one win of the ALCS
item.description: Rookie Braden Montgomery’s two-run double highlighted a three-run sixth as Chicago beat Cleveland 4-3 for a 2-0 ALDS lead. The White Sox have won four straight postseason games, all on the road, and can clinch their first ALCS berth since the 2005 championship season when the series moves to Chicago.

item.title: Cowboys stun Texans with a last-minute comeback
item.description: CeeDee Lamb caught a career-high 17 passes for 189 yards and scored the winning 12-yard touchdown with 40 seconds left as Dallas erased a 20-point deficit to beat Houston 34-30. The Cowboys scored 28 points after halftime, while the Texans fell to 0-4.

item.title: Chiefs hold off Raiders to remain the AFC’s last unbeaten team
item.description: Patrick Mahomes threw for 225 yards and two touchdowns, while Kenneth Walker III ran for 177 yards and two scores as Kansas City beat Las Vegas 30-27. The Chiefs improved to 4-0 and became the AFC’s final unbeaten team; the Raiders took their first loss.

item.title: Valkyries take Game 1 from defending champion Aces
item.description: Gabby Williams had 25 points, 11 rebounds and five assists as Golden State beat defending champion Las Vegas 71-60 in the franchise’s first WNBA semifinal game. Kiah Stokes added 14 rebounds and three blocks, and the Valkyries controlled the glass to seize a 1-0 series lead.
